pageCache.pageTitle: Shaftesbury Park Primary School - Our Vision and Mission
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Mission
At Shaftesbury Park, we develop children who:
Think about their world
We use the International Primary Curriculum to not just to teach children facts, but to develop inquisitiveness, creativity and curiosity about the subjects they are learning.
We use the International Primary Curriculum to build a connected understanding of the subjects in a global perspective, this enables us to develop inquisitiveness, creativity, and curiosity about their world.
Expand their world
We use the opportunities provided by our bilingual and enterprise classes to give the whole school a gateway to the wider world, helping children find the world beyond our borders, share similarities and celebrate differences
We use the opportunities provided by our bilingual and enterprise classes to give the whole school a gateway to the wider world, helping children find the world beyond our borders, share similarities and celebrate differences.
Change their world
We use the core enterprise values and the United Nations’ Convention on the Rights of the Child to help children develop the skills and values they will use throughout their life to make their world better.
We use the enterprise skills and the United Nations’ Convention on the Rights of the Child to facilitate the children in being able to actively make a difference now and enable them to see that they can be the change makers of the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Shaftesbury Park Primary School - Head's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Head's Welcome
Welcome to Shaftesbury Park, an award-winning, innovative community primary school in the heart of Battersea. Our diverse intake and inclusive ethos, based on our deep understanding of the United Nations Convention Rights of the Child, has enabled us to develop a mutually respectful and positive learning environment where our pupils are encouraged to play a valuable role in our school, the local community and the wider world.
Our use of an International Curriculum to teach subjects in a comprehensive, thematic and creative way instills international mindedness and encourages self-directed learning within our pupils. From this foundation, our children have the choice of learning in either a Bilingual or Enterprise stream. Our teaching is dynamic and ambitious, empowering our children to think about the world they live in, broaden their horizons and to contribute to causes that can change and improve their world. We are committed to developing an enterprising future generation that values the importance of mutual respect and cultural awareness and will be better equipped to confidently take their place in an increasingly global future.
We are proud of our success in the work that we do and in September 2018 we became the first school in the UK to be awarded the prestigious LabelfrancEducation, a quality seal from the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Development, granted to schools outside France with ‘French Bilingual Sections of extremely high quality’.
We are also the proud recipients of the British Council International School Award in recognition of our work to bring the world into the classroom and of our efforts to help all our pupils to develop the skills necessary for successful lives and careers in an increasingly global and interconnected world.
Since 2015, Shaftesbury Park has consistently been in the top 5% nationally in terms of pupil progress. We believe that our high academic results are the product of all that our school embraces, providing an optimum context where our children can make the best progress and reach the highest possible standards that they can in all aspects of their development.
Thank you for taking an interest in our happy and hardworking school.
© 2026 | Legal Information
Website design by Greenhouse School Websites

PTFA - Shaftesbury Park Parents, Teachers and Friends Association
Who We Are
The Shaftesbury Park Parents, Teachers and Friends Association (PTFA) brings together families, staff, and supporters who want to help every child at our school thrive. We work to strengthen the school community, create opportunities, and support the wellbeing and development of all pupils.
Our Aims
Raise Funds for the School: We organise events and activities throughout the year to raise money for resources, experiences, and improvements that directly benefit the children.
Build the School’s Profile and Reputation: We celebrate the achievements of our pupils and staff, promote the school within the wider community, and help make Shaftesbury Park a place families are proud to be part of.
Support Child Welfare and Development: We help enhance the learning environment, support wellbeing initiatives, and create opportunities that allow every child to grow academically, socially and emotionally.
Contact Us
Chair: Chair.Shaftesbury.Park.PTFA@gmail.com
Treasurer: Treasurer.Shaftesbury.Park.PTFA@gmail.com
Secretary: Secretary.Shaftesbury.Park.PTFA@gmail.com
What events would you like the PTFA to organise? Would you like to become a volunteer? Respond to our survey to share your thoughts: Link
Meet the PTFA Committee
Co-Chairs
Megan
Bio: Megan has two children at Shaftesbury Park and a third in secondary school. Native to California, Megan spent a year in Rennes, France as an exchange student, and speaks French at home with her children. Her children bring experience of two prior language immersion/bilingual education programs, which she hopes to leverage to further Shaftesbury Park’s mission. Megan is an engineer with experience in the aerospace and defence industry, and enjoys swimming, running, bouldering, and a good book.
Adam
Bio: Adam has a daughter in Year 1 Écureils (squirrels) and is better known around the playground as Caoilinn’s dad. He’s usually easy to spot at drop-off and pick-up in his fluorescent cycling jacket, steering the family’s trusty chariot (otherwise known as the cargo bike). A Civil Servant by profession, he enjoys bringing people and teams together to deliver positive outcomes. He loves a good coffee and is secretly hoping the school’s bilingual stream will help him improve his French too!
Peter
Hugo
Co-Secretaries
Katie
Bio: Katie is a mum to a bilingual stream son in Year 4. She works in the charity sector, providing help and advice to disadvantaged communities within Wandsworth, and is an avid fantasy and romance reader in her free time.
Aleksandra (Ola)
Bio: Ola is a mum to a bilingual stream student in year 6. Polish by origin, living now for several years in the UK, which she has always considered her second home. Her daughter is bilingual and the French language seemed a great idea to add to that set. Ola is a former teacher and currently a talent recruiter. Also known as a dog walker (a black flattie is easy to spot next to her. Always), and a manager of her daughter’s social and professional calendars. Together, they appreciate music, film, reading and sports.

pageCache.pageTitle: Shaftesbury Park Primary School - Enterprise Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Enterprise Curriculum
Enterprise Stream
At Shaftesbury Park Primary School, our Enterprise Stream is designed to equip children with the skills and mindset needed for future success. Starting from an early age, we provide opportunities for students to develop essential skills that will enhance their future employability and prepare them to become the entrepreneurs and leaders of tomorrow.
How We Teach the Enterprise Curriculum
Enterprise Education is integrated across all subjects, with a strong focus on the International Curriculum. This curriculum covers subjects like science, history, geography, music, art, technology, and PE, all tied together through engaging topics. Each topic is paired with a related theme from the Skills Builder programme, and approaches include:
For example, in the IPC topic "Saving the World," students might take on an Enterprise project like "Trash to Treasure," where they create eco-friendly toys from recycled materials to promote the importance of recycling.
Business Approach: Creating and selling a product.
Community Approach: Organizing events or exhibitions.
Environmental Approach: Running campaigns for a cause.
The 8 Enterprise Skills
The core of our Enterprise Stream is developing eight key skills that are essential for future success. These skills are woven into every lesson, ensuring that children have the opportunity to practice and master them over time.
Assessment
We assess each child's progress in Enterprise using the Skills Builder framework, which breaks down the eight employability skills into teachable steps. This framework helps us track each child’s development and make any necessary adjustments to our teaching methods to support their growth.
Beyond the Classroom: Building Enterprise Skills
We believe that learning doesn't stop at the classroom door. To further develop their Enterprise skills, our students participate in activities like:
Benefits of the Enterprise Stream for Children:
Collaboration with the Bilingual Stream
Although children are enrolled in either the Enterprise or Bilingual Stream, our school fosters a collaborative environment where both streams benefit from each other. Enterprise students gain exposure to French language and culture, while Bilingual students participate in Enterprise activities like Challenge Days. This collaboration enriches the learning experience for all students, both in and out of the classroom.
Our Enterprise Stream at Shaftesbury Park Primary School offers children a dynamic and engaging education that prepares them for a successful future, both academically and in their personal lives.

Maths Curriculum
Maths at Shaftesbury Park Primary School
At Shaftesbury Park Primary School, we use the Mathematics Mastery approach to help our students explore, understand, and enjoy maths. This method focuses on developing a deep understanding of mathematical concepts, so children can confidently apply what they learn in different situations.
What is Maths Mastery?
Maths Mastery is an approach that encourages students to understand the "why" and "how" of maths, rather than just memorizing formulas or methods. The curriculum is carefully designed to meet the 2014 National Curriculum for England, ensuring that all students cover the necessary objectives each year.

RSE Curriculum
Relationships and Sex Education
At Shaftesbury Park Primary School, we believe that relationships form an integral part of our Personal, Social, Health Education (PSHE) and Citizenship curriculum, and it is linked to the National Curriculum for Science which includes aspects of sex education. All content in the Relationships Education Curriculum supports the wider work of school in helping to foster pupil wellbeing and develop resilience and values that we know are fundamental to pupils being happy, successful and productive members of society.
Shaftesbury Park Primary School has a Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) Policy which aims to outline the place of Relationships and Sex Education within Shaftesbury Park Primary School, detailing how the subject is taught, the roles and responsibilities of staff, children and parents and parental rights to withdraw their children from this subject.

pageCache.pageTitle: Shaftesbury Park Primary School - Rights Respecting School
pageCache.text:
Rights Respecting School
Our school is proud to have sustained its Gold: Rights Respecting Award (RRSA), a prestigious accreditation that highlights our dedication to promoting and embedding children’s rights in all aspects of school life. Achieving Gold is a significant milestone, but maintaining it shows our ongoing commitment to being a rights-based community. This involves teaching about rights, through rights, and fostering an environment where pupils advocate for the rights of others.
By sustaining Gold, we ensure that children's rights are integrated into school policies, practice, and culture, benefiting pupils in multiple ways. First, it enhances their learning and well-being, creating an inclusive and supportive environment. Second, pupils develop a deeper understanding of global citizenship and social justice, empowering them to advocate for children’s rights both locally and globally. Finally, our students take an active role in driving progress through our RRSA Steering Group, honing leadership skills and shaping the future of the school.
Our commitment to sustaining Gold means that rights remain central to everything we do, from welcoming new students and staff to continuing our engagement with UNICEF UK and beyond. We are proud to uphold these values and look forward to reaccreditation to demonstrate our ongoing dedication to children's rights.

Governance Impact Statement 2025-2026
Governors
All schools are required to have a governing board and at Shaftesbury Park Primary School the board plays an important role in setting the school’s direction and monitoring performance. The governing board has three core responsibilities:
There are 5 types of governor at Shaftesbury Park: the headteacher is an automatic a member of the board, one staff governor is elected by the school’s staff, two governors are elected by parents, one governor is appointed by the local authority on the advice of the board and the remaining board members are appointed, or co-opted, by the board. All board members are equal, and are required to act in the interests of the whole school rather than representing any specific group. You can view details of terms of office and attendance.
Contacting the governors
Governors are always happy to hear from parents and other members of the school community. You can contact them through the school office, or by emailing the chair of governors at james.cousins@shaftesburypark.wandsworth.sch.uk
Who are Shaftesbury Park’s governors
Shaftesbury Park’s board is an active part of the school community, and includes members from school staff, parents, and co-opted governors appointed for the skills they bring to support the school’s success. You can find details of individual governors below:
Rebecca Caldecott (parent governor)
I have three children at Shaftesbury Park (currently in Years 6, 4 and 2) and they all started in reception. They are all in the bilingual stream, doing well academically, made great friends and are looked out for and supported when it has been needed.
I am not working at present but have a varied career over the last few years. For 15 years I helped run and educational trust that delivers international study courses across the UK and the world for professionals in the heritage sector. This helped me understand how education and administration needs to work effectively alongside each other.
Having experienced Shaftesbury Park as a parent I’m really enjoying seeing how it all operates behind the scenes. It works very hard to bring out the best in all the children with encouragement, sensitivity and pride in their achievements. We are lucky to have a school like this in our neighbourhood.
James Cousins (co-opted, chair of governors)
I have been a governor at the school for many years, first as local authority appointee and, more recently, as a co-opted member. and now have the immense privilege of being chair of governors.
Professionally my career started in the City, before moving into the local government and health sectors and then, more recently, consultancy work.
Within the school I’ve has taken a particular interest in the development of its unique curriculum offer and how — now it’s fully embedded — we can continue to develop both children and staff and fulfil the school’s mission of helping our children change their world.
Prof. Stephanie Hemelryk Donald (co-opted governor)
I have worked in higher education in Australia, Malaysia, and the UK for over 25 years with academic specialisms in Area Studies, International Studies, Film, and children’s media, with a focus on China, Europe, and migration. As well as leading academic schools and institutes across my career, I have also served as the Licensee of Murdoch Childcare centre (Australia), and as a link governor at Birkenhead Sixth Form College (UK).
I am now located in London, and I am keen to remain involved with education and excited to support the bilingual and enterprise approaches at Shaftesbury Park which are both progressive and practical, offering great value both to children and to the wider world.
Rachel Fleming (co-opted governor)
I became a governor at Shaftesbury Park in 2024 after looking for a way to be able to give some of my time to the local community. I was drawn in immediately by the ethos of the school. I believe that schools have the opportunity to do far more than just educate their pupils. Shaftesbury Park is an excellent example of a school that raises its children to be respectful of, and responsible for themselves, one another and their community.
I started my career as a modern languages teacher, before requalifying as a social worker. I have experience working for a London local authority, as well as within the NHS. I hope that the skills I have learnt through these roles will support the continued success of the school and its pupils.
Maya Haria (co-opted governor)
Ro Hulston (co-opted governor)
My governor journey at Shaftesbury Park Primary School has started in resources as it aligns professionally to my career pathway before being appointed to board. I hold a Master's in Business Administration from IE Business School. Currently I manage a global software sourcing team in an American multinational mass media and telecommunications organisation.I am very familiar with the UK education system as a parent, all my children attended similar schools in London and my mother was a primary school teacher. The school has a clear ethos and much to offer early years pupils and operates with a dedicated team, all of which I am keen to help succeed.
Philippe Mior (local authority)
Born in Belgium, I moved to the UK mid 2016.
I have worked in Banking and now Software consulting for the last 25 years where I gained a great experience in managing projects and budgeting. I strongly believe that education is one of the most important marker of success for a child’s life.
Jonathan Mogford (co-opted governor)
I joined the board of governors in 2025. I have lived here in the Shaftesbury Park Estate for thirty years and am delighted to have the opportunity to offer something back to my local community, especially supporting the growth and development of new generations for their futures. Having studied French at university, and having lived abroad, I am highly committed to the school’s dual bilingual and enterprise focuses.
Professionally, I have been a senior civil servant for many years mostly working on health, life sciences and regulatory policies in both national and international contexts. I’ve also non-executive experience with Citizens Advice (both in London and nationally) and with Age UK.
Celine Monteiro (parent governor)
I became a Governor at Shaftesbury Park in March 2025, shortly after my son started in Reception. I was keen to learn more about this great school and help it go from a gem that too few people know, to being famous for what it does: helping our children – all our children – think about the world, expand their world and change their world.
I currently work in the financial sector, leading large internal transformation programmes and client deliveries, and love the opportunity to put my skills at the service of the most important thing in life: our children.
I am really thankful to get to see, as a Governor and a parent, the amount of dedication, hard work and care from everyone to prepare our children for a bright and happy future.
Moya Wilkie (co-opted)
I have been a Governor since 2016: first elected as a Parent Governor when my child was in Year 1, and then co-opted after my initial term ended. I am a passionate believer in the importance of quality state education for every child, and as a local resident since 2005 I was pleased to have the opportunity to support Shaftesbury Park. Living in an English-speaking household, I was incredibly excited at the opportunities offered by the bilingual stream, and delighted to chair the Curriculum and Achievement Committee for 2 years.
I currently work in the charity sector but have a background in Higher Education administration and management, and have been able to bring skills in policy development, finance, and HR to the role of Governor. I am responsible for Safeguarding; working with our experienced staff team to keep Shaftesbury Park pupils safe and secure, and hence better able to make the most of their learning opportunities. I have been especially pleased to support the school’s Equalities work, creating an environment that is welcoming, respectful and supportive for all members of the school community.

pageCache.text:
Key Stage 2 Outcomes
We are very proud of our pupils’ achievements at the end of Key Stage 2. This year, our results show that children at our school continue to make strong progress across all subjects, performing in line with or above national averages in several areas.
Reading: Our pupils achieved particularly well in reading, with over 81% reaching the expected standard – higher than both the local authority and national averages. An impressive 42% of pupils reached the higher standard, showing excellent reading comprehension and enjoyment of literature.
Writing: In writing, our results remain strong, with attainment close to the local authority average and above the national figure for pupils working at greater depth.
Maths: Our children continue to develop their mathematical understanding, with many achieving the higher standard and demonstrating strong problem-solving and reasoning skills.
Combined Results: Overall, two-thirds of our pupils reached the expected standard in reading, writing and maths combined – above the national average.
These outcomes reflect our school’s commitment to high expectations, quality teaching, and a supportive learning environment that enables every child to succeed.

Information for Parents | Shaftesbury Park Primary School, Battersea
At Shaftesbury Park, we deeply value the partnership between parents, students, and teachers. We believe that working together leads to the best outcomes for our pupils, both academically and socially. Our open-door approach means that communication between home and school is always encouraged. We welcome parents to be actively involved in their child's education and development. Whether it’s through one of our curriculum open mornings or afternoons, regular meetings, events, or informal discussions, we are here to listen and collaborate with you.
We are proud to offer a unique school experience that goes beyond the traditional curriculum. As a Gold standard Rights Respecting School, we focus on instilling values of respect, equality, and inclusion in every child. Our students learn the importance of their rights and responsibilities, helping them grow into compassionate, global citizens.
Our international curriculum is designed to inspire a love for learning by embracing different cultures and perspectives. With a focus on bilingualism, we offer pupils the opportunity to become proficient in more than one language, preparing them for success in a globalized world. This approach not only enhances communication skills but also fosters creativity and critical thinking.
Additionally, our commitment to Enterprise education equips pupils with practical skills for the future. Through hands-on projects, they develop problem-solving, teamwork, and leadership abilities that will serve them well in all aspects of life.
We are located in South West London in Battersea and make to most of our locality. We are in close proximity to Clapham Junction and Clapham. We frequently visit sites in London such as The Natural History Museum, The Science Museum and Institut Francais (The French Institute) in South Kensington.
If you'd like to learn more about any aspect of our school offer, including our Rights Respecting School approach, International Curriculum, bilingual program, or Enterprise education, please don’t hesitate to contact the relevant lead teacher. We are here to support your child's learning journey and look forward to building a strong partnership with you.

Arbor Parent App
At Shaftesbury Park Primary School, a French / English speaking bilingual and Enterprise Primary School in Battersea, South West London, we use the Arbor Parent App to keep parents informed about their child’s life at school in a much more accessible way. Simply log into Arbor to see and update your child’s information and give consent for trips, photos/videos, etc!
How to get started
1. Wait for your welcome email from us telling you Arbor is ready - you won’t be able to log in before receiving this
2. Click the link in your welcome email to set up your password
3. Go to the App or Google Play Store on your phone and search ‘Arbor’
4. Click ‘Install’ on Android or ‘Get’ on iPhone then open the App
5. Enter your email, select the school, then enter your password
6. Accept the Terms & Conditions and enter your child’s birthday
Need help using Arbor?
In order to safeguard student data in line with the UK General Data Protection Regulations (UK GDPR), Arbor will only liaise directly with schools so if you have any questions about Arbor or need support with the App or Parent Portal, please don't hesitate to contact the School Office.
If you can, please tell us the type and model of your phone (e.g. an iPhone SE) and include screenshots or screen recordings to help us help you.

Lunchtimes
Lunchtime is essential for children to develop independence, social skills, and refuel for afternoon learning. Children can choose a hot school meal or bring a packed lunch. Meal choices can be changed each half-term with written notice to the School Office.

Two main meals (including a vegetarian option)
Fruit, yogurt, or a healthy dessert
Salad from the salad bar

Special Dietary Requirements
For children with special dietary needs, complete and return the Food Allergy and Food Intolerance Management Form available from the office.
Free School Meals
From September 2023, all children from Reception to Year 6 are eligible for free school meals. Parents must complete a Meal Arrangements Form to apply. This helps the school claim Pupil Premium funding, which supports enrichment activities and targeted support.
Packed Lunches
Children can bring a packed lunch. Please ensure it adheres to our Healthy School agenda and Packed Lunch Policy, available on the School Policies page. Packed lunches should be in labelled, non-breakable containers.
For school trips, packed lunches are free for children receiving free school meals. Order in advance using the Harrison Catering Packed Lunch Pre-Order Form that will be shared by staff.
Nut-Free School
Shaftesbury Park is a nut-free school to protect children with severe nut allergies. No nuts or nut products are allowed on school property.
For more information, please contact Debra Stocker at debra.stocker@shaftesburypark.wandsworth.sch.uk.

Payments
Scopay is our easy-to-use online payment facility, allowing parents/carers to make payments for school meals, school trips, extracurricular activities, extended day services and other miscellaneous items 24 hours a day, 7 days a week by either credit or debit card. Parents may also use this system to check credit balances, view their payment history and reprint any receipts. Communication regarding payments will be sent using this system.
Registration Instructions
If you don’t yet have a Scopay account:
Please visit the Scopay website and click ‘Register as a New User’.
Follow the instructions onscreen to enter your details and add the unique online link code for your introductory letter when prompted.
If you already have a Scopay account:
Please log in using the username and password you chose when registering your first child.
Select the ‘Link Accounts’ option from the ‘Your Info’ menu and enter the unique online link code from your introductory letter.
You can use the same account for any children you have at this school, and for children at other schools which also use the secure Scopay system. Simply follow the instruction above to create and link the accounts.

School Uniform
Our low-cost uniforms are designed to provide every student with a smart, cohesive look while keeping family budgets in mind. Made for both comfort and durability, they allow students to focus on learning without distraction. By promoting equality and school pride, our affordable uniforms help create a positive and inclusive environment where every student feels part of the school community.
Uniform Expectations for Zebra Nursery to Year 6
Collared navy-blue polo shirt (short- or long-sleeved) with the school logo
Red cardigan or sweatshirt with the school logo
Navy blue trousers or navy-blue school skirt
Plain dark socks (with trousers)
Navy-blue/red tights or white socks (with skirts)
Red/navy-blue hair accessories
Alternative Uniform Options (Summer term and Autumn 1 Half-Term only)
Tailored navy-blue shorts
Outdoor Clothing, Bags & Footwear
Plain navy-blue/black outdoor jacket
Optional reversible fleece/waterproof jacket with the school logo available
Shaftesbury Park School Bag with the school logo
Must be safe for running, playground games, and frequent use of staircases

How to Purchase School Uniform
Most uniform items are available from supermarkets and high street shops. Items with the school logo can only be purchased online.
Order by midnight on the 15th for delivery by the end of the month, or by midnight on the 30th for delivery by the middle of the next month.
Quick, secure, and easy
Excellent quality at competitive prices

Jewellery & Watches:

Only small stud earrings allowed; no additional jewellery. Face paint is permitted only on national fundraising/celebration days (e.g., Comic Relief, World Book Day).
